prospect.name: Rob
prospect.occupation: Deputy sheriff for his home county, 12 years, rotating 12-hour day/night shifts; retired from the US Air Force after 23 years; planning to retire from law enforcement in October and work part-time
prospect.family_status: Remarried around age 51; wife is 66, fully retired, vegan, active in church and sponsors an orphanage in the DRC. Five children aged 30-38, four grandchildren with one on the way. Youngest daughter marries in October.
prospect.training_background: Was in the best shape of his life roughly ages 40-49 training four to five days a week as a single parent; has not trained since remarrying around 12 years ago. Holds an unused gym membership, owns an unused elliptical and a home gym, and bought kettlebells a month ago that have never been touched. Currently walks his labrador briskly 2.5 miles most days on varied inclines and pedal-kayak fishes two to three times a week.
prospect.medical: Takes no medication other than a doctor-prescribed sleep aid that he says does not work. Reports chronic sleep deprivation over 12 years of rotating shifts - 'I've suffered with chronic sleep deprivation... it's absolutely miserable. And it's tearing me apart.' Self-reports BMI over 30, 'just probably sub-obese level'. Waist gone from 32 to 35 inches. States no injuries or physical limitations. Strong multigenerational family cancer history - mother died at 66 of kidney cancer, father at 62 of lung cancer. States he is not a proponent of radiation or chemotherapy and favours 'natural homeopathic cancer fighting protocols'. He and his wife were in a car accident; her hips and lower extremities were injured by the seatbelt and both went through chiropractic care, but he reports no lasting effect on himself.

signals: Explicitly wants a former self back: 'prior to getting married, I was probably in the best shape of my life... and then things just went south'
Carries visible regret and shame - 'I'm sick and tired of being sick and tired', 'to be able to take my shirt off at the pool with my grandkids without being self-conscious... It's embarrassing'
Lost ground to a hard season specifically identified: remarriage plus twelve years of rotating 12-hour shifts

Overlaps materially with the_preserver - 61, unusually health-literate, aging and longevity framing, retirement tightening liquidity - but the dominant drive is recovering lost ground rather than holding position

goals.text: Lose 25 to 30 pounds, back to where he was eight to ten years ago
Firm up and regain lean muscle - 'I don't want to be a bodybuilder. I just want things to be firm and less weight'
Be able to take his shirt off at the pool with his grandkids without being self-conscious
Fit into his suit for his youngest daughter's October wedding
Inspire his children and his wife to train, and get his wife on the journey with him
Age gracefully and stay active enough to enjoy retirement and his grandchildren
Reduce the risk of the cancer that has taken his family for several generations

pains.text: Chronic sleep deprivation across twelve years of rotating three-month day/night shift blocks; prescribed sleep medication does not work
Bought a gym membership, a home gym, an elliptical and kettlebells and has used none of them - 'all they are is collecting dust. I haven't even touched them'
Self-describes as in bad shape and sub-obese; waist up from 32 to 35 inches, lost lean muscle
Fear of the multigenerational family cancer pattern - 'the last several generations, no, they don't make it to even 70'
Embarrassment about his body around his grandchildren
Boredom snacking on night shifts and a self-described sweet tooth
Waiting on the October retirement as the moment things become possible - 'I hate to use that as an excuse and wait till then'
Wife is expecting him to take the lead and he has not; the kettlebells sit in the living room as a daily reminder

objections.raw_quote: we all have to pay bills, Richard. And that's something that certainly you have to prioritize and potentially commit to. As I transition and retire, of course, the budget is going to be a lot tighter.
objections.rep_response: Did not isolate or explore the financial picture at all. Instead volunteered an unsolicited price range - 'It would be in the four figures, somewhere between 1,000 and 6,000 or so' - and moved on to mobility questions.

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, we'd have to make the decision together.
objections.rep_response: Ran none of the scripted partner moves. Instead pivoted to including her: booked a second call for Friday and asked him to join on a laptop with her present so the process could be explained to both.

objections.raw_quote: I'm going to be retiring in October and I hate to use that as an excuse and wait till then because everybody, depending on your level of commitment should be able to carve out
objections.rep_response: Challenged it directly and immediately - 'I'm curious, Rob. Are you willing to also carve out that time at the moment?'

evidence: No offer was presented and no close was attempted; the rep deliberately deferred the pitch: 'I can explain the whole process to the two of you, and then we'll get started with you'
Second call booked for Friday at 1400 Florida time, contingent on the wife's availability: 'I'll coordinate with her. I don't know her schedule yet.'
Rep asked him to join from a laptop with the wife present
Counter-evidence for optimism: the prospect said his wife 'thinks I'm on a scam phone call right now', and confirmed only that he would confer and try to carve the time out
Positive signal: prospect committed on the call to pick up and dust off the kettlebell that day and message the rep when done
outcome.next_step: Joint call with Rob and his wife on Friday at 1400 ET on a laptop, where the process and price will be presented for the first time

notable.note: Two things a principal should see. First, the rep improvised a price range twice - '1,000 and 6,000 or so' and later '1500 to around six and a half for total, for six months' - neither of which is the published $6,000/$9,000 structure, and both delivered before any value had been built. The prospect wrote it down as '1500 to 5k a year' and takes that to a joint decision with his wife. Second, the rep confirmed on the record that a persona named Sophia messaging prospects is an automation and not a person, after the prospect had assumed she was a team member. Roughly the first ten minutes of the call were lost to Zoom camera troubleshooting and no frame was ever set.

quality.notes: Severe. The prospect joined from a phone and is labelled 'iPhone' throughout; his real first name (Rob) is only recoverable from the rep addressing him. Attribution inverts constantly - the rep's own questions ('How tall are you actually?', 'Why is it so important for you, Rob') are repeatedly filed under iPhone, and the prospect's answers under the rep. The Sophia exchange at 00:45:52-00:46:09 is badly scrambled and was reconstructed from content. Roles assigned from content throughout.
